researchQuestion: Do twelve genuinely distinct TDCC weekly vintage pairs guarantee an effective sample size of twelve when pair-level test statistics are serially dependent?
positiveMechanism: Using one pair-level effect rather than thousands of stock rows avoids cross-sectional pseudoreplication and preserves the IC110 frozen 12-pair observational requirement.
counterEvidence: Adjacent TDCC pairs share a vintage, and common regime shocks may induce positive pair-statistic autocorrelation. Distinct pair IDs do not prove iid pair effects.
alternativeExplanation: Measurement-noise differencing alone can induce negative adjacent correlation; sign and magnitude of actual serial dependence are UNKNOWN until real pair effects exist.

analyticResult.interpretation: Under assumed rho=0.5 AR1, twelve pair observations have the variance of approximately 4.5 independent equal-variance observations. This is only a conditional counterexample, not an estimate of TDCC behavior.

pitAndOosGuards: Require actual firstKnownAt, executableOpen and fifth-session-close for each admitted pair; do not infer from TDCC as-of date.
Any training label information interval touching the validation information interval is ineligible; no outcome-trained M0 coefficients may be reused as OOS predictions.
A chronology-based model must fit on prior fully matured labels only and retain immutable fit and prediction receipts.
If model fit and unique primary estimator remain ambiguous, report OOS_UNKNOWN and do not promote.
Do not count repeated consumers of one TDCC vintage pair as independent episodes.
